packageRules.description: Playwright's npm package and its container image must move together. The image ships the browser binaries built for that exact release, and a mismatch changes text rendering, which silently invalidates every visual regression baseline. Splitting them across two pull requests would leave the repository broken in between.
prBodyNotes: :warning: After merging, regenerate the visual baselines with `yarn docker:vr:update` and commit them. A browser update moves glyph rendering, so the committed baselines will no longer match.
Check that the Dockerfile tags in `env/docker/` and the `@playwright/test` version in `package.json` all name the same release.

packageRules.description: Agent definitions are generated from the installed Playwright version, so they drift when it moves.
prBodyNotes: Regenerate the agents with `npx playwright init-agents --loop=claude`, then re-append the project rules section each definition ends with.

packageRules.description: Linters and formatters land together. They are the static gate, they never affect what the suite tests, and reviewing them one by one is noise.
Workflow actions, kept current so the pipeline keeps running on a supported runtime. Node 20 leaving the runners is exactly the kind of change that arrives this way.
Allure reporting, grouped because the reporter and the command line generator have to agree on the results format.
